verdict: General Dynamics grew revenue 13% to $14.6B and profit 16% to $1.2B — and orders flooded in: a 6.8-to-1 book-to-bill took total backlog to $220B.

segments.name: Marine Systems
segments.note: Submarines and surface warships (Electric Boat, Bath Iron Works, NASSCO) — the fastest-growing segment on submarine production.

segments.name: Technologies
segments.note: Defense IT, mission systems and C5ISR technology and services.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.note: Gulfstream business jets and aviation services — 40 aircraft delivered in the quarter.

segments.name: Combat Systems
segments.note: Armored vehicles, weapons and munitions, mainly for the U.S. and European allies.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: General and administrative expense — the only running-cost line General Dynamics breaks out; everything else sits in the direct cost of its products and services.

otherDetail: Interest, net of $45M, partly offset by $4M of other income.
footerNote: General Dynamics reports a single 'operating costs and expenses' line of $13,039M. The split here follows its 10-Q: general & administrative expense of $722M is the running-cost block, and the remaining $12,317M is treated as the direct cost of products and services, so gross profit is revenue less that direct cost.

takeaways.title: Orders dwarfed deliveries
takeaways.text: The defense segments booked 8.5 dollars of orders for every dollar of revenue — a huge order intake, led by submarines — taking total backlog to $220B, including $98.8B in the defense segments' funded backlog growth story.

takeaways.title: Marine Systems is the growth engine
takeaways.text: Marine Systems revenue rose 21% to $4.96B and its operating earnings rose 34% as Columbia- and Virginia-class submarine work ramped.

takeaways.title: Cash conversion was strong
takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was $1.7B — 139% of net earnings — with free cash flow of $1.2B after $481M of capital spending.
